sophia: Heads up — prod saw a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate after the system-prompt tweak earlier today. 78% -> ~42% on the blue cluster. Profiling points at KV misses where the cache key differs only by tool_call ordering and a tiny system prompt suffix.

jake: Can you paste the profiler snippet and the differing cache keys? :eyes:

sophia: Sure — excerpt from the profile + logs:
```
cache_miss: key_hash=0x7f3a1b, raw_key={"system_prompt":"You are an assistant.","tool_call":{"name":"search","params":{"q":"x"}}}
cache_hit:  key_hash=0x9b2c4d, raw_key={"tool_call":{"params":{"q":"x"},"name":"search"},"system_prompt":"You are an assistant."}
// same logical payload, different JSON ordering -> different hash
```

maria: We did change the system prompt formatting to append a small telemetry tag (env+ts) — that could explain tokenization differences if tokenizers aren't pinned. We didn't include tokenizer/version in cache keys.

jake: Hypothesis: two simultaneous issues: (1) we compute cache key from the raw serialized prompt payload (includes JSON tool_call order + volatile system metadata), and (2) tokenizer/version is not part of the key. Fix plan: canonicalize tool_call JSON (stable key ordering), strip volatile fields from system prompt, and include tokenizer fingerprint in the cache key.

ana: Quick patch idea — pseudo-code for key_normalize:
```
def normalize_for_cache(payload):
  # remove volatile tool metadata
  payload.system_prompt = strip_timestamps(payload.system_prompt)
  payload.tool_call = deep_sort_keys(payload.tool_call)
  return json_dumps(payload, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)

cache_key = sha256(normalize_for_cache(req.payload) + tokenizer_fingerprint)
```

ana: I'll prototype this and run a small canary. Also adding a rule to drop tool_call.metadata.* (execution_id, client_ts).

ops-bot: deploy/patch-canary started: runtime v2.14.2 -> v2.14.3-canary (eng-runtime-blue). Tracking: prefix-cache-hit, p50/p99 latency, kv-miss-rate.

sophia: Good. After we roll the canary, let's run a prefix-warmup for the top 50 prefixes to refill KV and compare baseline. I can kick off the warmup.

jake: Warump command I used previously:
`./tools/prefill_prefixes --top 50 --model redwood-medium --tokenizer 2024-11-05-fingerprint`

maria: Also add unit tests that check ordering invariance: same logical tool_call with different key orders must produce identical cache key. And a test to ensure timestamps in system prompt are dropped.

ana: Opening PR with change, tests, and a benchmark harness. Assigning to @jake for review.

ops-bot: canary metrics after 20m: prefix-cache-hit increased from 42% -> 70% on canary nodes. No spike in p99. Monitoring for another 40m.

jake: Nice. If numbers hold, we'll roll to 10% -> 50% -> full with autorevert thresholds. Thanks everyone — please post any anomalies in this thread. :thumbsup:
